title: Stance at a Distance
author: Natalie Ashbridge, Cortne Edmonds, Stan Tunstall (Stern '21)
difficulty_source_label: Quant 4/10; Structure 7/10; higher dimension 7 mapped using round(7/2)
prompt: Our firm has just wrapped up a project with The Stance School, which offers K-12 education in Philadelphia, to help them with developing two major strategic initiatives. The first initiative, which is the priority, is an e-learning platform for their students to facilitate remote learning, in response to a global pandemic that resulted in students having to take classes from home for the last few months of the school year. The other initiative is a professional development tool to help the teachers with developing and effectively providing a remote curriculum to the students. The team that worked on the strategic planning determined that the cost would be $1M. You are now tasked with determining how these initiatives will be funded within the next year and whether or not the school should move forward with this project.

clarifying_info.answer: The case is set in first-half 2020. Launch at the start of 2020–2021 school year. Latest income statement is FY2018.
Stance is a private lower/upper K–12 school in a major U.S. city, with 1,000 mostly middle-to-upper-middle-class students. Approximately 10% receive scholarships.

Do not separately model ongoing program costs: the source says $1m annual savings should cover ongoing run-rate. Endowment is earmarked for specific purposes and long-term security and is unavailable for these initiatives.

interviewer_notes: Can also be administered interviewer-led in the supplied sequence. Guide toward revenue/expenses and internal funding, given the short deadline. Give Exhibits 1 and 2 together only when requested, then staffing Exhibit 3 and ratio Exhibit 4. Exhibit 3 is qualitative prioritization, not a demand to total every salary. If asked why payroll differs from the income statement, explain that salary/wages/benefits includes benefits typically about 50% of salary. If scholarships are proposed for cuts, warn that grant revenue would fall materially. After savings, prompt structured layoff-risk and gap-funding brainstorms if not volunteered. Source rewards at least 9 ideas with 1–2 creative examples but does not itself supply that many; do not invent required source answers. Either proceed or defer is acceptable with consistent reasoning.

suggested_framework.summary: Explore external funding and internal cash generation or cost reductions, respecting restricted funds.

tree.label: Fund the $1m initiatives within one year

children.label: Appropriations and grants, subject to eligibility
Endowment excluded after clarification because restricted

stages.interviewer_asks: How could Stance fund these initiatives within the next year?
stages.release_when: After the prompt; clarifications on request.
stages.info_to_release: $1m funding need; priority student platform plus teacher development.1,000 students, about 10% on scholarships. Private K–12 school; case dateH1 2020 and launch 2020–2021. Endowment unavailable; no separate ongoing-program-cost calculation needed.
stages.expected_answer: Consider internal revenue/savings and external public/private support. Given timing, investigate existing revenue and expenses first. Tuition, giving, grants, appropriations and loans are possible branches, but constraints must be checked; do not use restricted endowment.
good_answer_signals: Connects funding options to timing and restrictions.

stages.interviewer_asks: What do financial and enrollment benchmarks imply?
stages.release_when: Provide Exhibits 1 and 2 together when the candidate asks to evaluate finances.
stages.info_to_release: FY2018 line items and tuition/enrollment charts are supplied. Stance receives 100% of eligible grants; grants are not allocated to school expenses. Compare expense shares of tuition and fees. If scholarship cuts arise, explain that they would materially reduce grant funding.
stages.expected_answer: Stance has the highest tuition and declining enrollment, making further tuition hikes risky; additional eligible grants are exhausted. Normalize expenses to tuition/fees: Stance student services 15%, pay/benefits 35%, scholarships 30%, maintenance 20%; Rittenhouse 15%/25%/40%/20%; Chestnut 12%/23%/40%/25%. Pay/benefits is the largest Stance expense and disproportionate to peers. Investigate roles, salaries, headcount and staffing growth versus enrollment rather than compare absolute costs alone.
good_answer_signals: Uses revenue constraints to justify cost focus.

stages.interviewer_asks: Which staffing categories warrant closer examination?
stages.release_when: Give Exhibit 3 after identifying salaries as the priority.
stages.info_to_release: Role salaries, Stance headcounts and competitor average headcounts are in Exhibit 3. If asked about income-statement reconciliation, benefits typically add approximately 50% to salaries.
stages.expected_answer: Several non-teaching categories are above peers: administrative assistants, custodians, guidance counselors, IT technicians and librarians; teacher aides are also above peers. Teachers are below peers. Prioritize further investigation of roles with potentially lower academic disruption, not simply the largest gross savings. Request student-to-role benchmarks and assess effects on student support before reducing headcount. A guidance counselor or librarian is not automatically non-student-facing.
good_answer_signals: Balances efficiency with educational and mental-health impact.

stages.interviewer_asks: What annual savings result from meeting Exhibit 4's student-to-staff ratios?
stages.release_when: Provide Exhibit 4 after the staffing discussion.
stages.info_to_release: 1,000 students. Assistant: salary $45k,3 staff,500 students/staff. Custodian:$40k,17 staff,100/staff. Counselor:$65k,15 staff,100/staff. IT:$60k,6 staff,200/staff. Librarian:$50k,8 staff,250/staff. Exhibit 3 separately listed librarian salary $60k; use the specific Exhibit 4 calculation input $50k while flagging the conflict.
stages.expected_answer: Target headcounts 2,10,10,5,4 imply reductions 1,7,5,1,4, totaling 18 positions across 5 role categories. Salary savings are $45k+$280k+$325k+$60k+$200k=$910k annually. Gap to $1m is $90k before transition costs. This is salary-only: whether benefit costs are avoidable is not supplied, so do not automatically add 50% savings. Cutting 5 role categories does not mean eliminating every employee in those roles.
good_answer_signals: Uses student ratios rather than competitor averages from the prior exhibit.
Distinguishes salary run-rate savings from first-year net savings.

stages.interviewer_asks: What risks and costs accompany these reductions?
stages.release_when: After calculating savings; prompt if not volunteered.
stages.info_to_release: No quantified transition-cost data is provided.
stages.expected_answer: Financial risks include severance, pensions and union negotiations. Non-financial risks include timing of reductions and budget realization, adverse publicity, enrollment declines and student mental-health outcomes. Consider how reduced staffing affects implementation and services; structure the discussion rather than offering a laundry list.
good_answer_signals: Connects implementation timing and enrollment risks to available funds.

stages.interviewer_asks: How could Stance close the $90k salary-only funding gap?
stages.info_to_release: Baseline gap is $90k/year before transition effects or verified benefit savings.
stages.expected_answer: Options include lobbying for new appropriations, licensing the learning or training platform to other schools, paid remote tutoring or classes, donations from students/parents/alumni/others, and targeted high-net-worth gifts with naming opportunities. Existing grant eligibility is exhausted, so new appropriations or new programs should not be confused with unclaimed existing grants. Assess speed and feasibility before committing.
good_answer_signals: Returns to the original framework for additional funding routes.

stages.release_when: After funding, staffing and implementation analysis.
stages.expected_answer: Proceed conditionally if staffing changes are educationally acceptable and the $90k gap plus transition effects can be financed. The source identifies $910k annual salary savings from 18 positions in 5 categories. Validate benefits, severance, timing, enrollment and service effects; review contracts, confirm next-school-year savings and secure alternative support. Deferral is also defensible if reliable funding or student safeguards cannot be established, but consider the cost of missing needed remote-learning technology.
good_answer_signals: Gives a reasoned decision without claiming the full $1m is already secured.

exhibits.title: FY2018 income statement line items
exhibits.description: Values in USD thousands. Stance receives all eligible grants; grants are not allocated to school expenses. Table contains supplied line items, not calculated ratios.
exhibits.key_insight: Salary expense is unusually high relative to tuition; restricted grants do not provide an obvious unrestricted surplus.

exhibits.title: Tuition and enrollment trends versus peers
exhibits.description: Two unlabeled-point line charts for 2015–2019. Stance tuition rises from about $30k to $35k and is highest; its enrollment falls toward 1,000 while peers rise. Exact intermediate data points are not printed and are omitted rather than guessed.
exhibits.key_insight: Higher tuition alongside falling enrollment limits confidence in further price increases.

exhibits.title: Roles, salaries and peer headcount
exhibits.description: Supplied salaries and headcount benchmarks; librarian salary here differs from Exhibit 4.
exhibits.key_insight: Investigate overrepresented roles alongside educational impact, not salary alone.

exhibits.title: Student-to-headcount benchmark ratios
exhibits.description: Specific savings-calculation inputs for five role categories. No target headcounts or computed savings are included.
exhibits.key_insight: Divide 1,000 students by each ratio to determine retained staffing, then calculate salary savings.

math.question: How do expense ratios compare?
math.answer: Stance's pay/benefits ratio 35% exceeds peers 25% and 23%.

math.question: How much salary can be saved using Exhibit 4?
math.answer: $910,000 annual salary savings using the dedicated calculation exhibit.

math.question: What funding gap remains?
math.answer: $90,000 annual gap before transition costs and any separately verified avoidable benefits.

synthesis: Conditionally proceed if student services are protected and the remaining funding is secured. Exhibit 4 supports $910k annual salary savings from 18 positions across 5 categories, leaving $90k against the $1m target before transition costs. Confirm conflicting librarian salary data, avoidable benefits, contractual costs, timing and enrollment effects. Seek donations or appropriate platform-related revenue, review contracts and finalize next-year allocations. Deferral is reasonable if funding or educational safeguards remain unresolved.
what_great_looks_like: Normalizes costs to tuition instead of comparing school totals.
Balances staffing efficiency with academic and student-support consequences.
Returns to the funding framework when salary savings fall short.
common_pitfalls: Assuming grant headroom despite full eligibility utilization.
Using competitor headcount instead of the specific student ratios.
Adding 50% benefits to savings without establishing avoidability.
Treating run-rate salary savings as immediate first-year cash.

low_confidence_fields: exhibits[1].data (exact unlabeled yearly chart points omitted)
extraction.notes: All four candidate exhibits and two worked-answer pages visually inspected; images point only to candidate pages 76,77,79,81. Source inconsistency: librarian salary is $60k on Exhibit 3 but $50k on Exhibit 4; use the specific Exhibit 4 input for its requested savings, matching $910k/$90k source answers. Benefits are approximately 50% in a separate reconciliation note, but avoidable benefit savings are not specified. Exhibit 3 payroll totals $8.34m;50% uplift gives $12.51m versus $12.25m statement, consistent with approximate rather than exact 50% benefits. Source's 'eliminate 5 roles' means 18 positions across 5 categories, not every role-holder. School is explicitly private despite Public Sector label; client_type omitted because legal nonprofit/for-profit status is not stated. Source chart note says four schools though three are shown; no missing school invented. Difficulty uses higher rating 7 mapped to 4; math in math-stern-stance.py.
